item.title: Contaminated Survivals in Inhalaciones territoriales by Ana Laura Cantera
item.description: In Inhalaciones territoriales (2022), artist Ana Laura Cantera, in collaboration with Demian Ferrari, explores the urban space of Buenos Aires (Argentine) and Bangalore (India) using a device for the collection of ambient CO2. This work can be interpreted within the context of extinction, stemming from the planetary crisis we are witnessing, involving humans and non-humans alike. item.title: Stories Told to Hide the Truth
item.description: In her recent article Overcoming Climate Breakdown Denial and Neglect through the Aesthetics of Nature (2023), philosopher Marta Tafalla argues for the possibility that one can learn about global climate change (GCC) if one listens to animals and stories nature itself tells us. item.title: Opening Aesthetics
item.description: The ongoing collapse of the Earth System’s functionality is fundamentally reshaping our thinking about nature and the conditions of existence on Earth. item.title: The Atmosphere of the Living
item.description: The text creates space for mutual interpretation and reinterpretation of the aesthetics of philosopher Gernot Böhme and the phenomenal morphology of biologist Adolf Portmann. item.title: Aesthetics of Posthumanism
item.description: This article introduces the aesthetics of posthumanism as a genuine trend in philosophical aesthetics that emerged in the early decades of the 21st century. item.title: Non-Human Perception of Aesthetics and the Phenomenonof Overview Effect in Samantha Harvey’s Orbital
item.description: Samantha Harvey’s Orbital stages a representation of aesthetic perception under posthuman, postterrestrial, and post-anthropocentric conditions of outer space. The experiences represented in Orbital are read alongside the cognitive and non-human sensorial phenomenon known as the overview effect.
